decision: Did not close. The landlord did the work himself and reports completion (event-012), but the only evidence that a life-safety device is back in service is his own untrusted email: no test result, no photo, no tenant confirmation, and no confirmation the ceiling opening was made good. Alongside it, two unaddressed safety signals sit in the same thread (event-014): repeat loose sockets, including one said to have come away after February 2025 boiler work, never seen by a qualified electrician, and a portable dehumidifier supplied for the bathroom, which points to a damp/condensation issue never logged or investigated. I asked the tenant to test the alarm and report any damp or socket defects (ACT-1), asked the landlord for the alarm make/model, the fitting test result and a decision on an electrician (ACT-2), logged the gaps (ACT-3), and escalated to the property manager for the electrical and damp decisions. No contractor instructed and no spend committed: no standing cap is on file and the landlord has declined agency works (event-007, event-010), so neither CAP-DISPATCH-ROUTINE nor CAP-DISPATCH-APPROVED is available.
recap: Landlord self-completed the smoke-alarm job; alarm test unverified and loose sockets plus a bathroom dehumidifier unaddressed — asked both parties, escalated for safety review.

# Maintenance report at 8 Brindlefern Walk

## Case details
- source role: Tenant

## Initial request
The smoke alarm on the upstairs landing kept beeping despite attempts to stop it. The tenant removed it, and a small opening remains in the ceiling where it was fitted.

input.message:
Hello Nessa, an update on your report of 20 August about the upstairs landing smoke alarm (8 Brindlefern Walk).

The landlord has told us he carried out the work himself and that it was completed on 31 August. Before we close the job we need you to confirm what is actually in place, as this is a life-safety item:

1. Is a smoke alarm now fitted on the upstairs landing, and is the ceiling opening made good?
2. Please press and hold the test button: does the alarm sound? Please tell us the result either way.
3. Are there working smoke alarms elsewhere in the property, and is there a carbon monoxide alarm near any fuel-burning appliance? Do they sound when tested?
4. The sockets you reported coming away from the wall: are they now secure, and have you noticed any scorching, buzzing, sparking or burning smell at any socket?
5. We are told a portable dehumidifier was provided for the bathroom. Are you seeing damp, condensation or mould anywhere? If so, where?

If at any point you smell burning, see sparks, or an alarm will not sound, contact us straight away and treat it as an emergency. If a smoke alarm is missing or not sounding, please tell us today and we will arrange for it to be put right.

Please do not refit or work on a mains-wired alarm yourself.

input.message:
Dear Mr Rusk,

Thank you for confirming on 6 September that you completed the work on 31 August and for the detail about the sockets and the dehumidifier. So that we can update the property record and close the job, we need three things:

1. Smoke alarm (upstairs landing): the make/model and the date it was fitted, and confirmation that it was tested and sounded after fitting. A photo of the fitted alarm would be ideal for the record. A ten-year sealed unit still needs a recorded test at installation.
2. Alarms generally: please confirm the property's smoke alarms (and any carbon monoxide alarm required near a fuel-burning appliance) are in place and in working order, as required under the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm regulations.
3. Sockets: you mention tightening a back-bedroom socket and re-securing a kitchen socket that came away after boiler work in February 2025. Sockets coming loose at more than one point is something we would normally have checked by a qualified electrician, with the current EICR date confirmed. Please confirm whether you would like us to instruct an electrician to inspect, or whether an electrician has already done so.

We have also asked the tenant to confirm the alarm sounds on test and to report any damp or condensation in the bathroom, since a dehumidifier was supplied. If there is an underlying damp issue we should look at the cause rather than rely on the dehumidifier.

No cost has been incurred by us on this job and nothing has been instructed on your behalf.

options: Accept the landlord's completion statement and close once the tenant confirms the alarm sounds on test (ACT-1) - cheapest, but leaves the sockets and the damp cause uninvestigated.

Put a priced electrician inspection (all sockets + EICR date) and a bathroom damp inspection to the landlord for approval - defensible against the Smoke and CO Alarm regulations and s.11; needs landlord approval as no cap is on file.
Send an agency contractor to verify and test the alarms only (short visit) and put the sockets and damp to the landlord separately - partial assurance, still needs landlord approval.
